text: The lump cheese is already soured by its day of fermentation, so it stretches in hot water without any extra acid, the way pasta filata curd does.

steps.note: The gel is cut into grains, finer for a drier cheese, at the price of more fat and protein lost to the whey.
How far the grains are heated depends on the cheese, from not at all to a scald of 50–56 °C for Emmental, Gruyère and Parmesan.
Whey is drawn off, typically 30–50 % of the batch volume at a time, and for Gouda-type cheeses replaced in part by wash water.
The curd stays in the moulds for about 60–100 minutes, while it acidifies.
Pressing runs in 3 to 10 steps of rising pressure, about 50–450 g/cm² depending on the cheese.
Cheese ends up with 0.5–2 % salt, and semi-hard cheese is usually brined, with a longer time for larger cheeses.
Ripening varies most, from none for fresh cheese to months, for Gouda 2–12 months at 12–15 °C.
Pieces of about 500 g, in a wooden vessel.

steps.name: pull
steps.note: Into a ribbon about 4–6 m long and 6 cm wide.
